summary.intent: Use the GSD manager workflow to drive CipherBox milestone v2.0 to completion: verify/plan/execute the remaining closeout phases (69–79), ship completed phases through PR review, and specifically get PR #607 (Phase 74) past a real macOS-only Desktop-E2E failure before merging.
summary.outcome: Phases 69, 70.1, 74, 75, and 77 were completed and shipped (69/70.1 merged via PR #606; 74 merged via PR #607 after root-causing and fixing a genuine rotation/FUSE-T concurrency bug plus a token-TTL issue; 75 driven through the full ship-phase pipeline including a real SC3 crypto parity fix, with PR #608 opened and learnings commit in progress). Phases 76, 78, 79 remain unplanned and paused per user request.

repo: GSD's plan-file scanner (plan-scan.cjs:28) has a loose /PLAN/i substring fallback that miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' (e.g. '...WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md') as an extra plan, causing false 'partial/Executing' status even when a phase is 100% complete.

GSD's phase-completion predicate downgrades disk_status to 'partial' whenever plan_count > summary_count, and separately 'is_active' just means a file in the phase dir was touched in the last 5 minutes — not that an agent is actually running.

CipherBox has two incompatible wire-encoding domains that look identical at the type level: internal node-codec/stored sealed refs use base64, but ALL share-API wire fields (encryptedReadKey, encryptedWriteKey, itemNameEncrypted) are validated as hex via @Matches regex in every share DTO — nothing forces a call-site to pick the right one, so it recurs (bit CipherBox at least twice in this session alone).

write_sealed AAD binds node.generation() (crates/core/src/node/seal.rs), so any republish after a generation bump must re-seal the write body at the new generation using the stable write key — the rotation engine's write_sealed:None on rotated nodes silently broke this until fixed.

macOS FUSE-T/SMB's overwrite-rename issues an open() on the SOURCE file being moved; Linux's kernel rename never opens the source. This is why identical rotation/e2e tests pass on Linux/Windows and fail deterministically on macOS.

drain_refresh_completions in crates/fuse/src/fs.rs already guards mutated_folders/publish_queue folders from being clobbered by stale metadata refreshes (uses mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved which preserves keys instead of apply_owned_children which resets them) — but scope-exit rotation never marked its republished folders as mutated, so this existing guard didn't protect rotated inodes.

Building the desktop FUSE binary on this macOS host by default links macFUSE (/usr/local/lib/libfuse.2.dylib) instead of FUSE-T; must PKG_CONFIG_PATH-override with a FUSE-T-aliased fuse.pc placed first to reproduce CI's real macOS mount behavior.

API access-token TTL is hardcoded 15m (token.service.ts); headless desktop-e2e test binaries authenticate once at startup with no auto-refresh-on-401 and no Keychain refresh-token storage in test-login mode, so any E2E run exceeding 15m wall-clock 401-locks mid-suite — production's webview mitigates this with a UI refresh timer that the headless binary lacks.

CodeRabbit's macOS-only, JS `$` regex quirk: `/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/` without the `m` flag also matches a string with a trailing `\n`, causing CANONICAL_UUID_RE in packages/crypto/src/utils/encoding.ts to accept a 37-char 'uuid\n' that Rust's byte-length check correctly rejects — a real TS/Rust parity/soundness gap.

code.finding: rotate_read_on_scope_exit must mark all rotated folders (grant root + result.rotated_nodes) as fs.mutated_folders after refresh_rotated_inode_read_keys, so the existing drain_refresh_completions guard preserves freshly-rotated keys against stale in-flight metadata refreshes; without this, a concurrent refresh resets the file's inode read_key via apply_owned_children, causing parent/child key divergence and AES-GCM decrypt failures on retry.

re_mint_grants_rooted_at must hex::encode (not base64_encode) the share-grant encryptedReadKey field — the API validates it as hex via update-grant.dto.ts while internal node-codec fields (read_sealed, read_key_sealed) correctly remain base64; sending base64 here caused a 400 that fails rotation closed.
ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL made env-configurable (default unchanged at 15m in production) to allow desktop-e2e's long headless macOS runs (which include 120s+300s sync waits) to avoid mid-suite 401 lockout.

WinFsp handle_rename's overwrite-destination validation only checked non-empty-folder before this fix; ported fuser's kind-compatibility guard (ENOTDIR/EISDIR equivalents via new status_not_a_directory/status_file_is_a_directory NTSTATUS helpers) to reject file↔directory overwrite-renames, closing a Greptile-flagged P1 parity gap with the fuser rename path.

CANONICAL_UUID_RE regex check needed an explicit length guard (36 chars) because JS regex $ without the m flag matches before a trailing newline, allowing a 37-char 'uuid\n' string to pass where Rust's is_canonical_uuid_form (aes.rs:159) correctly rejects via bytes.len() != 36.

workflow: When a background/scheduled agent claims success ('all cargo/typecheck green'), independently reproduce or spot-check before trusting the claim — CI's Typecheck job caught a real gap (mock fixtures not updated for a widened type) that vitest's non-type-checking transpilation missed entirely.

For a suspicious CI-only failure, replicate locally first rather than theorizing — building the actual FUSE-T binary, resetting the full 3-layer stack (Kubo+DB+journal together, since partial resets desync), and instrumenting with targeted debug logs (rather than guessing) took ~10 runs but converged on the exact root cause where three prior 'fixes' (write_sealed preservation, FilePointer self-heal, coalesced dest-gate) all failed.

Sub-agents launched at the repo root cannot EnterWorktree into a pre-existing worktree ('repo root, not an isolated worktree' error) — the working pattern for parallel background phase work is sequential processing on the main checkout switched per feat branch, not worktree isolation for sub-agents.

Before dismissing a CI failure as 'infra flake,' extract the actual failure signature from the log (not just adjacent warning noise like 401s) — the user's pushback correctly identified that the real failure was 'no write_sealed body' + EACCES + an explicit 'dest-gate rejecting a legitimate overwrite (regression)' message from the test harness itself.

Instrumenting with targeted debug print/log statements at 3-4 specific decision points (key fingerprints, gate decisions) is far more effective for pinning nondeterministic-looking cascading failures than re-running and re-theorizing; each hypothesis (API resolve lag, stale captured key, coalesced exclusion) was individually falsified by one instrumented run before landing on the true cause.

When a GSD todo auto-close mechanism under-closes (leaves resolved todos in pending/), cross-check `resolves_phase` tags against the actually-shipped code/tests rather than trusting the pending/completed split — 3 stranded phase-74 todos were found and moved during phase-75 shipping.

friction: Repeated hex-vs-base64 encoding confusion across the codebase caused the SC#2 grant re-mint 400 error — a systemic issue acknowledged by the user as recurring ('this has happened before'), leading to a dedicated high-severity hardening todo rather than a quick fix.

Multiple session/quota limit interruptions (at least 3: ~02:48, ~07:35-09:40, ~09:50-13:xx) required scheduling cron-based autonomous resumes with increasingly corrected instructions after the first resume strategy (EnterWorktree into existing worktrees) proved fundamentally broken.

Initial crypto-privacy sub-agent review got the hex/base64 encoding backwards for shares.rs (called correct hex doc-comments 'base64'), showing the encoding domain confusion affects careful reviewers too, not just implementers.

The macOS Desktop-E2E root-cause investigation required ~10 full local reproduction cycles (~10 min each) across multiple false leads (write_sealed preservation, FilePointer self-heal, coalesced dest-gate, API resolve lag) before landing on the correct fix (marking rotated folders as mutated_folders).

Fixing the Part D rotation bug immediately surfaced a second, unrelated latent bug (15-min access-token TTL causing 401 lockout) because the fix let the macOS suite run long enough to cross the token-expiry boundary — required a second full CI cycle to isolate and fix.
Response stalled mid-stream twice during long agentic tool-call sequences, requiring the user to nudge continuation ('please continue with the /ship-phase 75 flow').
